openings.name: Italian Game
openings.idea: One of the oldest openings. White develops the bishop to c4, eyeing the f7 square — Black's weakest point in the opening.
plans: Build a strong center with c3 and d4.
Castle kingside early and bring the rook to e1.
Target f7 with the bishop and a knight jump to g5 in some lines.
openings.counter: Black equalizes with the solid Giuoco Pianissimo (…Bc5, …Nf6, …d6) or counterattacks with the Two Knights (…Nf6). Keeping e5 defended and completing development neutralizes White's pressure.

line.note: Grab the center and open lines for the bishop and queen.
Develop with a threat — you hit the e5 pawn.
The Italian bishop. It aims straight at f7, Black's soft spot.
Prepare d4 to build a big pawn center.
Strike in the center now that it's supported.

openings.name: Ruy López (Spanish)
openings.idea: White pins the knight that defends e5 and pressures Black's structure. A deeply strategic opening favored for over a century.
plans: Pressure c6/e5 and prepare c3 and d4 for a big center.
Reroute the b1-knight via d2-f1-g3.
Play for a long positional squeeze.
openings.counter: The Berlin Defense (…Nf6) steers into a solid endgame. The Morphy Defense (…a6) questions the bishop; after Ba4 Black gets a flexible setup.

line.note: Claim the center.
Attack e5 and develop.
The Spanish bishop pins the defender of e5 and pressures c6.
Keep the pin alive rather than trading on c6.
King safety first; the e4 pawn is indirectly defended.

openings.name: Queen's Gambit
openings.idea: White offers the c4 pawn to deflect Black's d5 pawn and dominate the center. Not a true gambit — White usually regains the pawn.
plans: If Black takes (…dxc4), play e3 and Bxc4 to regain the pawn.
If Black declines (…e6), build with Nc3, Nf3, pressure d5.
Use central space for a queenside minority attack.
openings.counter: The Queen's Gambit Declined (…e6) is rock-solid. The Slav (…c6) supports d5 while keeping the bishop free. Both are world-championship mainstays.

line.note: Take central space with the queen's pawn.
Offer the gambit — challenge d5 and open lines.
Pile up on d5.
Pin the f6-knight to add pressure on d5.
Open the bishop and keep a solid, flexible center.

openings.name: Slav Defense
openings.idea: Black supports d5 with the c-pawn instead of the e-pawn, keeping the light-squared bishop free to develop outside the pawn chain.
plans: Develop the c8-bishop to f5 or g4 before …e6.
Hold the center and aim for …dxc4 with …b5 to keep the pawn.
Castle and seek a sound, flexible structure.
openings.counter: White presses with Nf3 and Nc3 and can try an early e4 push. Central space and quick development keep White's initiative alive.

line.note: Meet the center head-on.
The Slav move — support d5 but keep your light bishop free.
Develop and reinforce d5.
Grab the pawn; you can try to hold it with …b5 later.

openings.name: Sicilian Defense — Najdorf
openings.idea: The most famous Sicilian. …a6 prepares …e5 or …b5 and denies White the b5 square. Black fights for the initiative, not just equality.
plans: Expand on the queenside with …b5.
Develop flexibly: …e5 or …e6.
Counterattack rather than defend.
openings.counter: White tries the English Attack (Be3, f3, Qd2, O-O-O, g4) or sharp 6.Bg5 / 6.Bc4, racing to attack the king first.

line.note: The Sicilian — fight for the center asymmetrically.
Support a future …e5 and open the c8-bishop's diagonal.
Trade off White's d-pawn to get the half-open c-file.
Develop and hit e4.
The Najdorf move — control b5 and prepare …e5 or …b5.

openings.name: French Defense
openings.idea: Black challenges the center with …d5. Solid and strategically rich, though the c8-bishop can be hard to develop.
plans: Undermine White's center with …c5 and …f6.
Find activity for the light-squared bishop.
Play on the queenside where Black often has space.
openings.counter: White gains space with the Advance (3.e5) or trades in the Exchange (3.exd5). The Tarrasch (3.Nd2) keeps a flexible, slightly freer game.

line.note: Prepare …d5 without committing the c8-bishop yet.
Strike the center directly.
Immediately attack the base of White's pawn chain.
Pile up on d4, the chain's base.

openings.name: Caro-Kann Defense
openings.idea: Like the French, Black hits the center with …d5, but prepares it with …c6 so the light-squared bishop can develop freely first.
plans: Develop the c8-bishop actively before …e6 locks it in.
Keep a sound structure and aim for a good endgame.
Trade into safe, solid positions.
openings.counter: White tries the Advance (3.e5 Bf5) for space, or the Classical for quick development, pressing Black's slightly passive setup.

line.note: Prepare …d5 while keeping the light bishop's path open.
Challenge the center on your terms.
Open the position and remove White's central pawn.
Develop the bishop actively — the whole point of the Caro-Kann.

openings.name: London System
openings.idea: A reliable system: White sets up the same solid structure (d4, Bf4, e3, Nf3, Bd3, c3) against almost anything. Easy to learn, hard to crack.
plans: Build the London pyramid: c3-d4-e3, bishop on f4, knight on f3.
Castle kingside and expand carefully.
Rely on structure over theory.
openings.counter: Black contests the f4-bishop (…c5 and …Qb6 hitting b2 and d4) or frees the game with an early …Bf5 / …c5.

line.note: Start the London with the queen's pawn.
The London bishop — develop it outside the pawn chain before e3.
Solidify the center and open the f1-bishop.
Complete the setup; next comes Bd3 and c3.
Keep your good bishop by stepping back from the trade.

openings.name: Scandinavian Defense
openings.idea: Black challenges e4 at once. After the queen recaptures and retreats, Black gets a solid, straightforward structure with little heavy theory.
plans: Develop quickly: …Nf6, …c6, …Bf5 or …Bg4.
Castle and aim for a sound middlegame.
Avoid early queen harassment.
openings.counter: White develops with tempo against the exposed queen (Nc3, d4, Nf3, Bc4) and enjoys a lead in development and central space.

line.note: Challenge e4 immediately.
Recapture — yes the queen is out early, but she'll find a safe home.
Retreat to a5, out of the way but still active.
Develop and prepare to castle.

openings.name: Nimzo-Indian Defense
openings.idea: Black pins the c3-knight to fight for e4, often trading the bishop for the knight to damage White's structure in return for central control.
plans: Double White's c-pawns with …Bxc3 when it brings lasting gains.
Blockade the light squares and control e4.
Trade the dark-squared bishop for structural concessions.
openings.counter: White picks the Rubinstein (3.e3), Classical (4.Qc2 to avoid doubled pawns), or Sämisch (accept doubled pawns for the bishop pair). Bishop pair and center vs structure.

line.note: Flexible development, controlling e4.
Open the f8-bishop's path.
The Nimzo pin — fight for e4 and threaten to damage White's pawns.
